verdict: In its first year owning Interpublic, Omnicom's revenue reached $6.4B and profit rose as merger savings started to land.

segments.name: Advertising & marketing services
segments.note: One revenue line: media buying, advertising, PR and other agency services billed to clients — including pass-through client costs billed back at cost. The Interpublic (IPG) agencies, acquired in November 2025, are included for the full quarter.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Agency overhead beyond the people who serve clients directly.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on offices and equipment, plus amortization of acquired intangibles — much higher since the IPG deal.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $133M less $29M of interest income — a net $104M cost. Equity-method earnings of $2M are folded into the same step, so the chart shows net other expense of $102M.
follow100Note: Cost of services is mostly the pay of the agency staff who serve clients, plus client costs billed through. This quarter it includes $85M of merger severance and repositioning costs and a $107M gain on businesses held for sale.

takeaways.title: Underlying growth is solid, not +59%
takeaways.text: Reported revenue jumped 59% because IPG is now included. In core operations, organic growth was 7.2% — healthy for a global agency group.

takeaways.title: Merger savings are the story to watch
takeaways.text: Omnicom says it is on track to deliver $900M of cost savings from the Interpublic combination — the main reason profit can grow faster than revenue.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EBITA margin widened
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITA was $1.1B, a 17.6% margin — up from 16.1% a year ago on the combined basis — as savings began to offset integration costs.

oneTimers: Operating costs include $84.7M of severance and repositioning costs tied to the Interpublic (IPG) merger, and a $106.8M gain on assets held for sale and dispositions — the two roughly offset this quarter.
Year-ago comparisons are Omnicom alone: IPG closed on November 26, 2025, so reported growth rates mostly reflect the acquisition.
footerNote: Net income shown ($675M) is before $19M attributable to noncontrolling interests (attributable: $656M).
